intro: IBPS PO runs in three stages: a qualifying Preliminary exam, a merit-deciding Main exam and a Common Interview. The notification names each test with its question count, marks and timing, but does not itemise a topic-wise syllabus.
note: The topic lists below are the conventional scope of IBPS PO papers mapped to this site's subjects; treat them as a study map and check the official notification for the final word. Structure per the CRP PO/MT-XVI notification: Prelims is 100 questions for 100 marks in 60 minutes with a separate 20-minute timer per section and weighted marking (English Language 30 questions for 30 marks, Quantitative Aptitude 35 for 30, Reasoning 35 for 40). Mains is 170 objective questions for 200 marks in 160 minutes (Reasoning 40 questions for 60 marks in 45 minutes; General, Economy and Banking Awareness with Digital and Financial Awareness 50 for 60 in 35 minutes; English Language 40 for 20 in 35 minutes; Data Analysis & Interpretation 40 for 60 in 45 minutes), followed by a two-question, 25-mark, 30-minute Descriptive Paper typed on screen, which the notification says may be scored by an automated mechanism. One-fourth of the marks assigned to a question are deducted for each wrong answer.

sections.name: English Language
topics: Reading comprehension (passages with questions on main idea, inference and vocabulary in context)
Fill in the blanks (single and double)
Synonyms and antonyms, idioms and phrases
sections.tip: Mains English carries only 20 marks from 40 questions (0.5 per question), so speed matters more than depth there. The Descriptive Paper (essay and comprehension) is where written English is scored in earnest.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude (Prelims) / Data Analysis & Interpretation (Mains)
topics: Data interpretation: tables, bar charts, line graphs, pie charts, caselets and missing-data sets
Percentage, ratio and proportion, average and ages
Time and work, pipes and cisterns
Time, speed and distance, trains and boats
Arithmetic word problems on the above topics
sections.tip: In the Mains this section is named Data Analysis & Interpretation: 40 questions for 60 marks in 45 minutes (1.5 per question), dominated by DI sets. In the Prelims it is 35 questions for 30 marks in 20 minutes.

sections.name: Reasoning Ability
topics: Puzzles and seating arrangement (linear, circular, floor-based, scheduling, box and tabular)
Statement and conclusion, statement and assumption, course of action
Critical reasoning: arguments, inference, cause and effect
sections.tip: Reasoning carries the heaviest weight in both stages (Prelims 35 questions for 40 marks, Mains 40 for 60), and puzzles and seating arrangements take up roughly half the section in recent papers.

sections.name: General, Economy and Banking Awareness with Digital and Financial Awareness
topics: Current affairs of roughly the last six months, weighted toward finance and the economy
RBI circulars, policy and payment systems
sections.tip: Mains only: 50 questions for 60 marks in 35 minutes (1.2 per question). The official test name explicitly includes Digital and Financial Awareness, so RBI notifications and payment-system news are scored areas.

sections.name: Computer Awareness (no separate test in the current pattern)
sections.tip: There is no separate computer test under the CRP PO/MT-XVI structure; digital banking and payments are tested inside the General Awareness paper. Use this list as background for that section and the interview, not as a separate scoring section.
